security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline method names, and normal Python import examples in SKILL.md. I confirmed one high-risk issue: the Direct Line key listing example prints channel keys to output, which could expose a bot secret if copied against a live Azure tenant. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found in the skill text.

remediation.issue: Direct Line keys are printed in example output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the key print statement or show masked values only. Add guidance to store keys in Azure Key Vault.

remediation.issue: The skill includes examples that create, update, delete, and configure Azure resources.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings to run examples only in a test subscription or with least privilege permissions.

remediation.issue: OAuth connection examples include placeholder client secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep secrets in Azure Key Vault or environment variables and avoid writing them into prompts, files, or logs.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Bot Service with Python
content.value_statement: Azure Bot Service setup often requires many SDK calls and resource details. This skill gives focused Python examples for managing bots, channels, and OAuth connections.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install Azure Bot Service and Azure Identity Python packages.
Demonstrates authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and subscription environment variables.
Provides examples for creating, reading, updating, listing, and deleting bot resources.
Shows channel setup for Microsoft Teams, Direct Line, and Web Chat.
Includes examples for OAuth connection settings and common service operations.
Summarizes supported client operations, SKU options, and channel classes.
limitations: Examples require an Azure subscription and permissions to manage Bot Service resources.
The skill does not deploy or host the bot application endpoint.
Placeholders must be replaced with tenant-specific values before use.
Generated guidance may need updates for SDK version changes.

use_cases.title: Provision Bot Resources
use_cases.description: Create and update Azure Bot Service resources from Python management scripts.

use_cases.title: Configure Bot Channels
use_cases.description: Set up Teams, Direct Line, or Web Chat channels with the management SDK.

use_cases.title: Review Bot Operations
use_cases.description: Map available client operations, SKU choices, and connection settings before automation work.

prompt_templates.title: Start Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to authenticate to Azure Bot Service with DefaultAzureCredential and environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan the Azure Bot Service SDK steps to create a bot in an existing resource group.

prompt_templates.title: Add Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding Teams, Direct Line, and Web Chat channels to an existing Azure bot.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Bot Service automation plan for safe secret handling, least privilege access, and cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need to create a new Azure bot with the Python SDK.
output_examples.output: The response outlines authentication, resource group selection, bot properties, SKU selection, endpoint setup, and post-creation checks.

output_examples.input: I want to enable Teams and Direct Line channels.
output: A channel setup sequence with required resource names and channel identifiers.
Notes about Direct Line key handling and safe storage.
Validation steps to confirm each channel is enabled.

output_examples.input: I need to audit my bot management script before running it.
output_examples.output: The response highlights destructive operations, secret exposure risks, subscription scope, and recommended test environment checks.

best_practices: Use least privilege Azure roles when running management examples.
Store app secrets and channel keys in Azure Key Vault or a managed secret store.
Test create, update, and delete operations in a non-production subscription first.
anti_patterns: Do not print Direct Line keys, OAuth secrets, or app credentials to logs.
Do not run delete examples against production bots without a confirmed recovery plan.
Do not paste live tenant secrets into prompts or shared documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps generate and explain Python SDK workflows for Azure Bot Service management tasks.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a user may adapt and run separately.

faq.question: Which Azure authentication method is shown?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential from the Azure Identity library.

faq.question: Can it help configure bot channels?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Teams, Direct Line, Web Chat, and references other common channel types.

faq.question: Does it manage bot application hosting?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Bot Service management resources, not application hosting or deployment.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use a managed secret store and avoid printing keys, OAuth secrets, or application credentials.
